newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil hits more contract lows, soy down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil hits more contract lows, soy down.

text.p: Big losses in soybean futures helped push all CBOT soyoil months to make new contract lows again Friday, and soymeal futures also ended lower.
"Soyoil is such a dog of a market right now," said one soyoil trader. "Even the crushers haven't been in this market lately."

Soyoil futures garnered some support earlier from talk of fresh U.S. export business. Cash traders said China bought a 20,000-tonne U.S. cargo of soyoil for July shipment and other sources reported interest in U.S. soyoil from some North African countries.
Heavy supplies of soymeal in U.S. cash markets and waning feed demand pressured soymeal futures and cash basis offers on Friday, traders said.
July contracts remained under pressure from liquidation ahead of first notice day on Monday. Traders are expecting heavy deliveries of 3,000 to 5,000 lots of soyoil and no soymeal deliveries.
July soymeal ended $1.70 per ton lower at $262.20, and other months were $0.60 to $2.40 lower. July soyoil settled down 0.16 cent a lb at 22.20, and other months ended down 0.04 to 0.13.
The weekly National Oilseed Processors Association crush report came in near trade expectations and provided little direction to prices, traders said.
NOPA reported a weekly crush of 24.223 million bushels and trade estimates ranged from 23.95 to 24.50 million.
In soymeal trade, Merrill Lynch sold 300 lots July and Smith Barney sold 400 lots August. ADM bought 200 lots August and Continental Grain bought 200 lots July, pit traders said.
In soyoil trade on the day, Produce Grain bought 200 lots August and Merrill Lynch sold 100 lots August and 300 lots July, pit traders said.

Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 32,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 29,879 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 30,000 lots, against Thursday's actual volume of 36,219.
